  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Reminders: Being reminded of the event by others, Avoid Authority Figures: Being around people in authority or uniform, Smoking: I smoke
  Threat: Waking Alert: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe, Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly, Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

Vignette:
Julio Hernandez's eyes would snap open in the dead of night, his heart racing as he lay there, listening for any sign of movement. It was a habit that had formed over months, ever since the memories of the torture he endured in his home country began to resurface. He would wake up, drenched in sweat, and get out of bed to check if all the doors and windows were locked, just to reassure himself that he was safe. This ritual had become so ingrained that even on nights when he was working a double shift as a maid at the hotel, he would find himself getting up from his breaks to patrol the empty corridors, making sure no one was lurking in the shadows. It had been three years since Julio escaped the clutches of his captors, but the memories still lingered, vivid and raw. He remembered the sound of screeching tires as they threw him into the back of a car, similar to the ones he would see driving down the streets every day. The sight of those cars would send a shiver down his spine, transporting him back to that moment when his life was turned upside down. Media reports of human rights abuses in Latin America would also trigger flashbacks, and Julio would find himself glued to the TV, reliving the trauma all over again. People around him couldn't understand why he became withdrawn whenever they asked about his past or brought up the topic of torture. "Don't remind me," he'd say, trying to brush it off, but deep down, Julio was terrified that if he let his guard down, even for a moment, the memories would come flooding back and consume him whole. Julio's fear wasn't limited to specific triggers; it had become an integral part of his daily life. He would avoid walking alone at night, sticking to well-lit streets and crowded areas, always on the lookout for potential threats. Strangers approaching him, even in ordinary situations like ordering food or asking for directions, would set off alarm bells in his head. His friends and family couldn't comprehend why he was so jumpy all the time, but Julio knew that it was just a matter of time before someone discovered his true identity and came after him. As a maid at the hotel, Julio had learned to navigate the labyrinthine corridors with ease, always keeping a watchful eye out for any signs of trouble. However, whenever he encountered authority figures – security guards, police officers, or even immigration officials – Julio's instincts would kick in, telling him to flee or hide. It was as if his mind had created a direct link between uniforms and danger. Despite the chaos brewing inside him, Julio found solace in smoking. It was a coping mechanism he had developed during his captivity, when cigarettes were used as a tool of manipulation by his tormentors. Now, whenever anxiety crept in, Julio would light up, letting the nicotine calm his frayed nerves. Positive emotions confused Julio; they made him feel vulnerable and exposed. Whenever someone showed him kindness or affection, he'd pull away, unsure of how to respond. His divorce a year ago had been a painful reminder that even love couldn't protect him from the darkness within. Julio's world had shrunk significantly since the trauma, but what finally brought him to seek help was the realization that his fear was starting to seep into his relationships with those he loved. He was tired of living in constant alertness, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. As he sat in the therapist's office, Julio knew it wouldn't be easy to confront his demons, but he hoped that by facing them head-on, he might finally find some respite from the memories that haunted him.
